blocks.text: Willingdon Heights: streets and boundaries

items.t: Willingdon Heights is the residential grid around Willingdon Avenue south of Hastings Street, and Heritage Burnaby describes it as a primarily residential commuter neighbourhood shaped by its closeness to the Trans-Canada Highway, Lougheed Highway and Hastings Street.
Willingdon Heights Park, at 1491 Carleton Avenue, is the in-area park, and its outdoor fitness circuit is one of the few City-listed facilities inside the grid itself.
Kitchener Elementary, at 1351 Gilmore Avenue, serves the area's west side; Burnaby North Secondary, at 751 Hammarskjold Drive, is the secondary school northeast of the grid.
The Brentwood Town Centre lands at the northeast corner of Lougheed Highway and Willingdon Avenue form the area's southern commercial edge.

blocks.text: Willingdon Heights: the housing stock

items.t: The stock is detached houses on the Carleton Avenue, Gilmore Avenue and Parker Street grid, with the Brentwood towers rising at the Lougheed Highway edge — two housing worlds on one street pattern. Heritage Burnaby's record frames the area as primarily residential and commuter-oriented.
Confederation Park, a short way northwest, is the area's full-service park: 3 tennis courts, 10 pickleball courts and the covered Sohen Gill Sports Box.

blocks.text: Willingdon Heights: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Lots near Brentwood Town Centre Station sit in a Frequent Transit Network Area pattern: the City states that within those areas in the R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) District, up to 6 dwelling units may be built on lots of 281 square metres or more, and off-street parking is optional.

The Brentwood Town Centre Development Plan (1996) is the City's community plan for the town centre at this area's south edge, and Council authorised a consultation in January 2024 to amend it and the Brentwood Site Conceptual Master Plan (adopted 2013).

Where the 1996 plan and the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan (OCP) disagree, the OCP's land-use map now takes precedence — the City's community plans page states this applies city-wide since the OCP's adoption on December 9, 2025.

blocks.text: Willingdon Heights: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Hats Off Day closes this area's main street: the City's events material describes the street party hosted by Burnaby Heights merchants on Hastings Street, with the City's own environment booth at Carleton Avenue and Hastings Street.
Willingdon Heights Park's fitness circuit is genuinely old equipment kept in service — the City calls the stations "vintage" bodyweight stations, unlike the new circuits in Central Park.

A new Confederation Park Community Centre is in planning northwest of the area: the City describes it as a new centre within Confederation Park to meet growing recreation needs in northwest Burnaby, with the project page updated October 27, 2026.
The R2 extension brought eight new bus stops and Expo and Millennium Line connections to the Willingdon corridor, per TransLink's launch summary.

blocks.text: Willingdon Heights: development and new projects

items.t: Brentwood Town Centre Plan Amendments and Brentwood Site Conceptual Master Plan amendments, Willingdon Avenue at Lougheed Highway, City of Burnaby: proposed changes add the City's Rental Use Zoning Policy (2020) housing, a publicly accessible green space and child care on the Brentwood site, and redesignate the Willingdon-and-Lougheed parcel from commercial to mixed-use residential and commercial. Status: consultation authorised January 29, 2024, open house held April 2, 2024, amendments in progress (as of November 3, 2026).
Brentwood Community Centre, Brentwood Town Centre, City of Burnaby. Status: listed as "Planned" on the City's projects page (as of November 3, 2026).

Brentwood pedestrian and cyclist railway overpass, five candidate streets including Willingdon Avenue, City of Burnaby. Status: Phase 1 feasibility complete; Phase 2 draft designs scheduled for late 2026 (as of November 3, 2026).

The Amazing Brentwood towers by SHAPE at 4567 Lougheed Highway sit in the Brentwood Town Centre, south of the railway — named here once; the full project entry belongs to the Brentwood pages, not this residential grid.

blocks.text: Willingdon Heights: costs and taxes

items.t: The Metro Vancouver Regional District portion of a 2026 Burnaby residential tax bill is $0.05440 per $1,000 of taxable value, under Schedule 2 of the Burnaby Rates Bylaw 2026, Bylaw No. 14814.

A mixed-use or storefront property on Hastings Street can also be charged the Hastings Business Improvement Area local service tax named in the same rates bylaw — a cost a purely residential Willingdon Heights house does not carry.

blocks.text: Willingdon Heights: getting around

items.t: The R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus is now the corridor service: Park Royal to Metrotown Station via Phibbs Exchange, Hastings Street and Willingdon Avenue, 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. daily since September 7, 2026.

TransLink's April 2026 announcement adds that the R2 serves Burnaby Heights, BCIT's (British Columbia Institute of Technology) Burnaby campus, Brentwood Town Centre and Metrotown, and that construction ran through summer 2026.
The 130 remains the local-stop bus on Willingdon Avenue, stopping at Brentwood Station on the Millennium Line between Kootenay Loop and Metrotown Station.

blocks.text: Willingdon Heights: risks and due diligence

items.t: The active railway south of the grid is the named constraint: it is why the City is studying overpasses, and a buyer on the streets nearest it (Parker Street, Georgia Street) should expect train noise that no City page quantifies — the overpass study page discusses crossings, not noise levels for individual lots.

Plan-change risk is live here: the Brentwood plan amendments could redesignate the Willingdon-and-Lougheed parcel to mixed-use residential and commercial, changing what can be built at the area's south edge — check the current plan status before pricing a lot on development potential.

Still Creek runs along the area's southeast near Brentwood Station; lots toward Still Creek Drive should be screened on the City's Riparian Management Areas layer for a Streamside Protection and Enhancement Area before planning an addition.

blocks.text: Willingdon Heights home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

18 houses sold in Willingdon Heights with a median price of $1,704,000 (the middle half sold between $1,604,375 and $2,121,500), taking a median of 20 days to sell at 97.6% of the last list price; 33% sold above list. They had a median $694 per square foot, a median year built of 1980 and a median lot of 4,059 square feet. 8 townhomes sold in Willingdon Heights with a median price of $1,090,000 (the middle half sold between $966,750 and $1,381,250), taking a median of 12 days to sell at 97.0% of the last list price; 12% sold above list. They had a median $796 per square foot, a median year built of 2005 and a median strata fee of $623 a month.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Willingdon Heights?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 17 houses and 17 condos and townhomes listed in Willingdon Heights. Those are month-end counts and they move daily, so ask Jared for a current list.

faq.q: Is Willingdon Heights a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 6% (a buyers’ market); condos and townhomes had 12% (a balanced market). The sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed; on the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers. One month in one community is a small sample, so look at the monthly table above before you decide.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Willingdon Heights from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 8 houses and 8 condos and townhomes sold in Willingdon Heights over those 5 months; detached houses peaked in June with 3 sold and condos and townhomes peaked in July with 3 sold.

faq.q: How big is Willingdon Heights compared with the rest of Burnaby?
faq.a: In October 2026, Willingdon Heights held 4.0% of the 430 detached houses listed in Burnaby and 1.3% of the 1,309 condos and townhomes listed in Burnaby.

faq.q: What mix of houses and condos is for sale in Willingdon Heights?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses made up 50.0% of the 34 homes listed in Willingdon Heights and condos and townhomes made up 50.0%; of the 3 that sold, houses were 33.3% and condos and townhomes 66.7%.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Willingdon Heights than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses was little changed, 17 in June and 17 in October 2026 (+0.0%); condos and townhomes rose from 13 in June to 17 in October 2026 (+30.8%).

faq.q: What changed on Willingdon Avenue transit in fall 2026?
faq.a: The R2 Marine–Willingdon RapidBus was extended from Phibbs Exchange to Metrotown Station on September 7, 2026, running via Hastings Street and Willingdon Avenue past this area. TransLink states it runs 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. daily, every six to seven minutes at peak, and it replaced the peak-only 222 Willingdon Express, which was discontinued.

faq.q: Is the 130 bus still the local option on Willingdon?
faq.a: Yes, with a change: TransLink's 2026 fall service changes keep the 130 providing local service on Willingdon Avenue, but most trips now start or end at Kootenay Loop, with only select weekday peak trips continuing to Phibbs Exchange. Its timetable runs from Phibbs Exchange via Hastings Street, Willingdon Avenue (Brentwood Station) and Central Boulevard to Metrotown Station.

faq.q: Why is there talk of an overpass near Brentwood?
faq.a: The City is studying a pedestrian and cyclist overpass across the active railway in Brentwood, at five candidate locations from the Brentwood Town Centre Development Plan: Madison Avenue, Alaska Street, Willingdon Avenue, Beta Avenue and Douglas Road. Phase 1 is complete and Phase 2 design feedback is scheduled for late 2026, so no crossing is built yet.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Carleton Avenue home?
faq.a: Kitchener Elementary at 1351 Gilmore Avenue is the west-side elementary, and Burnaby North Secondary at 751 Hammarskjold Drive is the area's secondary school building.

faq.q: What did houses in Willingdon Heights sell for?
faq.a: 18 houses sold in Willingdon Heights between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $1,704,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Willingdon Heights?
faq.a: The median was 20 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.6% of the last list price (33% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
